_note: 牛肉（和牛）の系譜。銘柄牛と、すき焼き・焼肉という食べ方の系譜を同じ表に置く。planned の行の era は出典が付くまで「—」
name: Wagyu and beef

cells.what: Tajima cattle, Hyōgo-born and raised, that pass a grade
cells.rule: A/B 4+ with marbling BMS 6+, 28–60 months; about 7,000 head a year; sold only through registered shops with a bronze statue
cells.price: Lunch steak ¥8,020 (round) to ¥21,780 (A5 sirloin) at a Kobe house
cells.howToEat: Steak on a teppan, or sukiyaki

cells.what: Virgin heifers of the Kuroge breed fattened longest in the Matsusaka area
cells.rule: Brought in by 12 months, tracked by ID; 'Tokusan' = Hyōgo calves fed 900+ days (GI 2017)
cells.price: Sukiyaki-cut 300 g ¥7,050 from the oldest house's shop
cells.howToEat: Sukiyaki at Wadakin, the house that made the name

cells.what: Kuroge cattle raised longest in Shiga; the oldest beef-eating tradition in Japan
cells.rule: Certified Ōmi = A4/B4 and up (GI 2017); shipped as 'Kobe beef' via the port in 1879
cells.price: Sukiyaki-cut 500 g ¥4,320–10,800 from a certified shop
cells.howToEat: Sukiyaki, shabu-shabu, and the Hikone miso-cure

cells.what: The closed bloodline behind Kobe, and the seed stock of most Japanese Kuroge

origin.era: an English teacher took one to Yokohama, 1875

cells.what: Kuroge heifers from the Okitama district, 33 months and up
cells.rule: Grade 3+ (GI 2017); about 20% above the Tokyo market average

cells.what: Thin beef cooked at the table with sugar and soy, dipped in raw egg
cells.rule: Kanto simmers in warishita broth; Kansai sears the meat first, then seasons — but Kyoto's oldest house uses a broth
cells.price: ¥8,200 at the 1868 Yokohama house; ¥13,530 set at Imahan; ¥1,430–3,190 at a chain

cells.what: Grill-it-yourself beef, a Korean-Japanese creation; tongue-with-lemon from the 1970s
cells.rule: 'Rōsu' and 'karubi' are menu names, not cuts, by the trade's own admission; ID numbers posted by law
cells.howToEat: Smokeless grill since 1980; one-person counters since 2018
